The structure connects a quality-and-duty-cycle deployment envelope to resource mechanisms, then to three workloads, data-flow/integration choices and total task economics. It does not use hardware names as chapter substitutes or convert peak speed into a recommendation. Sections 2-3 distinguish weight residency, working memory, KV state and OS/application reservations, then explain which optimizations change memory, bandwidth or computation and where quality must be checked. The document chapter follows parsing through retrieval, grounded generation and citation validation; interactive generation separates phase-specific latency, history growth and device contention; the speech chapter follows capture, VAD, overlap, recognition and endpointing. This gives each workload a sufficiently detailed mechanism and prevents a clip benchmark from standing in for live partial results or sustained thermal behavior. Section 7 traces documents, excerpts, embeddings, transcripts, logs, synchronization and fallback across local/cloud boundaries; section 8 carries quality, hardware, energy, support and network assumptions into conditional decisions. Shipping API restrictions, heterogeneous runtimes and updates therefore affect recommendations rather than appearing as an unrelated appendix. The proposed fit matrix and worksheets preserve conditions and evidence types, and historical MELT mechanisms are explicitly separated from forecasts for newer hardware. ODM-U1 supplies conditioned premises, ODM-U2 constructs task envelopes and ODM-U3 performs calculations and synthesis.
